verdict.rationale: The Microsoft 365 Copilot overview lists "Copilot Chat in Outlook and Teams" and describes interacting with Copilot over web and work data (Microsoft Graph and Work IQ), so an AI assistant does exist inside Teams. The evidence is only a thin mention, though, and doesn't show users actually handing off tasks to it. The agent-building docs (Agents Toolkit, slash commands, streaming) are developer building blocks for custom agents, so they earn no credit here. Missing for 10: documentation of what tasks Copilot can carry out in Teams (e.g. summarizing meetings, drafting messages, taking actions on the user's behalf), detail on how delegation works in the Teams UI, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
